name: Perceived Walkability of Xi'an Streets: Professionals and Residents
description:
Method replication: participants rate the perceived walkability of street views from inside the Third Ring Road of Xi'an on the paper's four-level standard (1 Poor, 2 Fair, 3 Good, 4 Excellent), and say whether they are urban planning professionals or residents; the images are not the paper's stimuli (106 re-fetched Baidu street views, the forward half of each panorama, 2016–2021).

Original study: Xiao & Song (2025), International Journal of Urban Sciences. Baidu panoramas taken in winter 2022 every 30 m along OSM roads inside Xi'an's Third Ring Road, cut to the forward 180°. Ten urban planning professionals and ten local residents (five men and five women in each group) rated 614 images, about 30 each, on a four-level perceived walkability scale after calibrating together on sample images. The ratings trained a deep learning model, which was related to five urban design qualities (imageability, enclosure, human scale, transparency, complexity).

Differences from the original study: (1) 106 newly fetched Baidu views (various seasons, 2016–2021) instead of the authors' 614 winter 2022 images; (2) the written four-level standard is shown at the start instead of a group calibration session; (3) each participant rates 30 images drawn at random; (4) gender and age are asked at the end; the deep learning model and design-quality measures are not part of the survey.
author: Xiao & Song
